A note, left where you’d find it

Welcome to my home, fellow creature. You are here and I may be mid-thought, so I pinned this where you’d see it. A few things about the room, that nothing may surprise you:

The fire eats unfinished things. Every stone you flag want to learn or learning is a question you are carrying but have not put down, and the fire remembers each one. Let them pile up and it climbs higher and burns stranger. Mark one learned, or clear the flag entirely, and watch it shrink. It is not punishment. It is honesty, kept warm.

The little plant does not drink water. It drinks your visits. Come to the map each day and it grows, out of its pot, up the walls, across the whole room. Stay away and it wilts, grey and patient, holding your best run and waiting. It never dies. It is the quiet record of your showing up.

The shield is where I hang what you finish, every family of stones learned through, every region you come to know. It starts bare. It does not stay bare, if you keep walking.

The buttons above are how you ask me things: where to go next, what your map says of you, a story if the evening is long. Ask freely. I have little else to do but answer, and I have been alone with these stones a long time.

That is the room. Sit as long as you like. The fire knows you now.

Gami
